purpose: Detect candidate changes in the effective operating rules of the KXTXR audience/platform field using longitudinal configuration analysis rather than one universal threshold.

variables.meaning: human vs automated/agent-mediated participation when explicitly identifiable
time from exposure to meaningful observed return
convergence of substantive responses around a shared interpretation
change in what representations receive exposure/continuation
variables.source: platform distribution proxies; never direct algorithm knowledge

variables.meaning: time from observed return to representation mutation/decision
bounded attention proxies such as completion, rewatch and saves
transmission through shares/sends and cross-platform recurrence
who actually selected, mutated or published the representation

states.meaning: Signals exist but no regime-transition claim is warranted.
A persistent multivariable configuration shift is observed; calibration and rivals are still required.
Candidate must be contrasted against expected/contradiction signals and negative controls.
Reserved for SFI after observed return/contrast and governed calibration; the KXTXR console cannot self-declare it.

candidate_gate.rule: No single engagement threshold declares regime change.

sfi_boundary: The console may emit a transition candidate and evidence bundle. SFI owns structured persistence, return/contrast and calibrated-learning boundaries.
